question: Explain the main reasons why companies undertake mergers and acquisitions.
sources: Generally accepted corporate finance principles on mergers and acquisitions
Companies Act, 2013, Sections 230 to 232 (compromises, arrangements and amalgamations)

points.label: Operating synergy
points.description: The combined firm is worth more than the two separately through economies of scale and scope, shared facilities and lower costs, or higher combined revenue.

points.label: Financial synergy
points.description: Better use of surplus cash, greater debt capacity and possibly a lower cost of capital for the combined business.

points.label: Growth and market position
points.description: Faster growth than building internally, entry into new markets or regions, larger market share and reduced competition (subject to competition law).
points.basis: M&A principle: external growth and market power

points.label: Diversification and resources
points.description: Spreading business risk across products or markets, and gaining technology, brands, licences, talent or raw material sources.
points.basis: M&A principle: diversification and access to resources

points.label: Tax and other benefits
points.description: Tax law allows a successor, in specified amalgamations and subject to conditions, to use accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation of the merging company; revival of sick units is another motive.
points.basis: Income-tax law provisions on carry forward of losses in amalgamation (conditions apply)
